input.quote: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes liquidated damages payable by us (Customer) to Vendor at USD 25,000 per day for "any delay in providing a dependency" — no materiality threshold, no notice or cure period, and no aggregate cap. This fails the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and also fails the fallback, which tolerates only an early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount; this is a per-day penalty untethered to termination. It is close to walk-away territory because an accumulating daily amount triggered by minor delays can exceed remaining contract value, and the mutual cap in § 21.1 gives limited comfort (it is set at the greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000, i.e. potentially well above annual spend, and the § 7.3 withholding right covers disputed Fees rather than damages claims). We propose deleting the clause, offering day-for-day schedule relief instead.

proposal.summary: Delete the USD 25,000/day liquidated damages payable by Customer for dependency delays
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages against us: our playbook does not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by the Customer, and this one is uncapped, applies to any delay however minor, and carries no notice or cure period. If Vendor needs protection for dependency delays, we can instead agree a day-for-day extension of affected timelines and relief from related Vendor service commitments.
